title: Atomic age: mid-century Space-Age retro-futurism - editorial and poster covers, ads and labels in cream, teal, vermilion, mustard and charcoal, plus mission documents (flight plans, checklists, orbital plates, credentials)
summary: Two linked grammars on one palette. A) Atomic-age editorial and poster: cream paper, one vermilion main colour against teal, mustard and charcoal; condensed lowercase or caps titles in two inks, geometric tracked caps, starbursts, orbit ellipses, boomerangs, a sun disc, swept rockets as flat glyph silhouettes, Googie scenes in image slots, halftone and misregistered plates. B) Mission documents: typewriter mono on white sheets, a vertical time ladder (a tick a minute, a long one every ten), ruled edition tables, punched holes, rubber stamps, unsigned ballpoint ticks, orbital diagrams, white-line plates on black and press credentials. Marks (logos, insignia, emblems) are image slots the owner fills; they are never drawn.

provenance.case: atomic-age kit (examples/atomic-age-kit): an original world, the Halcyon Orbital Lines and its survey office, filled into all ten templates on one print-set sheet, plus a landing page in the grammar (1440 and 390 wide). The showcase sheet carries real historical text (programmes, dates) where the owner asked for it; the pack's defaults stay original.
provenance.lineage: Mid-century Space-Age retro-futurism: 1950s-60s magazine covers, travel and science posters, car-brochure ads, cloth-bound technical books, and the flight plans, checklists, diagrams and press credentials of the early crewed space programmes. Read and measured on an owner-supplied mood board of 17 panels (palette clusters, light shares, visual-weight centres, proportions of mastheads, discs, rockets, ladders and tables); the board stays private and is not shipped. Borrowed: the grammar and the measured proportions. Never borrowed: logos, insignia, emblems, wordmarks, pictures or proprietary fonts.
provenance.borrow: Borrow grammar, never assets. Every default name and line in the templates is our own (Orbitville Gazette, Halcyon Orbital Lines, Meridian 88, Halcyon 7); marks are empty image slots with a size and clear-space rule; rockets and satellites are flat glyph silhouettes in code, realistic scenes are image slots with task sheets.
provenance.rounds: template check --browser on every template at every size with the OFL fixtures, and on the kit's print-set sheet and landing page (1440 and 390): first pass and final counts in the PR.

fonts.substitution: The board's faces are mostly period metal and photo type (condensed grotesques, a geometric sans of the Futura family, a Didone masthead, typewriter faces). Open stand-ins: League Gothic for the condensed titles (its lowercase is narrower and less contrasted than the board's masthead), Jost for the geometric caps (Futura's proportions; the board's tracked wordmark is wider-set), Courier Prime for the typewriter (cleaner than a worn IBM ribbon, no ink spread), Caveat for annotations (a felt-pen hand, rounder than the ballpoint). The Didone masthead line (VAULT) has no open match in the catalog at this weight; the pack sets that line in Jost Bold tracked instead. fonts query reports none of these families because the catalog holds CJK-capable families only; each face is named with its OFL source and read from --font-dir.

grammar: Two grammars, one palette. Editorial and poster screens are cream (paper L 85-88) or a dark ground (charcoal, navy) carrying one vermilion main colour; documents are white sheets (L 87-90) with charcoal type only, plus ballpoint and stamp inks.

Vermilion is the main colour: the sun disc (0.216 of the cover width), the ad field (35-45% of the panel), the poster band, the hot half of a two-ink masthead, the solar print's ground. Teal is second (blocks, labels, the cool half); mustard plays plates and the field-guide ground; charcoal is structure.

Titles are condensed: a masthead at 0.17 of the cover height in two inks inside one word, a poster title slanted, three stacked caps lines on a book; geometric caps are tracked wide (0.52 em on the ad wordmark, 0.08-0.18 em on taglines).

Motifs: four-plus-four ray starbursts with dots at two tips, thin orbit ellipses crossing the frame, boomerang shapes, a sun or planet disc, one swooping line on linen; rockets and satellites only as flat glyph silhouettes with straight trail lines.

Print: cream paper aged at the edges, halftone shading on discs and planets, a second plate misregistered by 2-8 units (mustard behind vermilion); real ageing, halftone and misregistration come from materials generate and process.

Documents: a time ladder with a tick every minute and a long tick every ten (labels :10 ... :50, hh:00 on the hour), bracket and dotted rails, typed blocks at their minute, a boxed checklist, a six-column edition table (MISSION, EDITION, DATE, TIME, DAY/REV, PAGE), punched holes along the top (five) or side (three), rubber stamps at -7 to -12 degrees.
Scale contrast of 1:10 or more on every template (masthead against page numbers about 1:14; ad year against wordmark tracking 1:3 in size but 1:12 against the logo note).
Marks are slots: logos, insignia, emblems and seals are image slots with a stated size, safe area and clear space; the code never draws a mark.

procedural: starbursts, orbit ellipses, boomerangs, discs, linen weave, a code dot screen on shapes (layouts-atomic.cjs)
swept rocket, classic rocket and satellite glyphs: flat silhouettes in a few polygons (sweptRocket, classicRocket, satellite)
time ladder, bracket and dotted rails, ruled tables, punched holes, rubber-stamp frames
recipes: Aged paper for the `paper` / `board` ground slots: materials generate --generator paper --params '{"profile":"wove-cream","tint":"#EAD5B0","age":1.2,"foxing":1.5,"stains":1,"creases":1,"width":1500,"height":2000,"pxPerMm":4}' --seed 3 (record kept in materials/generated).

Printed vermilion flat for the solar print: materials generate --generator print --params '{"profile":"litho-red","ink":"#B03D1C","paper":"wove-cream","margin":0,"misregisterMm":[0.6,-0.4],"second":"#E8922A"}' --seed 2.

Halftone and misregistration of a scene in an art slot: materials process --file materials/raw/<scene>.png --effect duotone --params '{"inks":["#211E1B","#17555B"],"angles":[45,75],"misregisterMm":[0.5,-0.3],"periodPx":7,"paper":"wove-cream"}' --seed 1.
Realistic scenes (Googie architecture, launches, Earth and Moon) come from a public-domain period source (materials fetch) or an image-generation task sheet (#311); never drawn in code (#301).
collage: Pictures sit in image slots with a ground plate under any text; marks sit in their own slots with clear space.
materials.sources: Everything else is drawn; pictures and marks are your own files in image slots.

motionNote: Print grammar: no motion of its own. On a page, reveal sections with a 240 ms ease-out rise of 12 px; a starburst may turn 15 degrees in 1.2 s on hover; nothing blinks.

guidance: 64 px distinctiveness (guidance): shrink each render to 64 px tall beside the other packs and the private board; a cover should read as cream with a vermilion disc and a two-ink masthead, a poster as a dark field with a planet limb and a light diagonal, a document as white with a black ladder rail.
Never draw a logo, insignia, emblem, seal or wordmark: fill the mark slot with the owner's file and keep its clear space.
Never draw a realistic vehicle, person or building in code (#301): rockets and satellites stay flat glyph silhouettes; scenes go in image slots with task sheets.
Annotations are unsigned: no signatures, no handwritten notes attributed to a real person, no quotes or endorsements.
Latin roles take Latin, digits, ASCII punctuation and – — ‘ ’ “ ” • · ° × … ©; mixed CJK copy goes in a body slot (glyph coverage).
Render with --font-dir holding the pack's faces: titles are sized from the face that renders, so without them the condensed titles fall back to Noto Sans SC at a smaller size.
checks.note: Run --browser for halftone patterns, image grounds and rotated stamps (the static half reads geometry only).
